data.hypothesis: Assigning contiguous x coordinates to each warp should improve coalescing relative to the baseline's four-x-wide tile. Having each thread produce four consecutive y outputs lets it reuse a 12-row neighborhood in registers and removes shared memory and barriers; the extra global load requests per output and register use may offset those gains, so correctness and full-run latency need controller measurement.
data.notes: This candidate preserves the coefficient expression and the baseline halo mapping: rows below zero map by +63 and rows at or above 64 map by -63, while stored row 63 remains distinct. It keeps one kernel launch and adds no allocation. The available baseline evidence (baseline-e1) is correct with mean latency 3.494 μs; this candidate has not been measured, so no speedup is claimed.
transformations: Replace the shared-memory derivative kernel with a no-shared-memory kernel whose warp lanes cover contiguous x elements.
Compute four consecutive y outputs per thread and load their 12-row union once for register reuse.
Retain the baseline's exact coefficient arithmetic and period-63 halo mapping, including the distinct stored endpoint row.
Launch a 32-by-2 block with an 8-output y span per block and a grid over x, y groups, and z; keep one launch and allocate no additional storage.
